store: Bergstrom Market: Neighborhood grocer in a dry county. Full produce and dairy departments, small butcher counter. Does not sell alcohol of any kind.
Halvorsen Provisions: Mid-sized independent market. Good selection of local beers and Minnesota ciders, plus a small wine wall. Produce is ordinary.
The Green Larder: Strictly vegetarian grocery. Broad produce, tofu and seitan, bulk grains and nuts. Does not sell meat or fish.
Dockside Grocery: Harbor-front market. Sells fish, whole and filleted, landed the same morning. Pantry goods are minimal.
Pinecrest Foods: Rural supermarket. Carries a full butcher counter with beef, pork and poultry. No seafood counter — does not sell fresh fish.
Saint Anne's Cheese: Cheesemonger. Deep in raw-milk and aged cheeses, cultured butter, crème fraîche. Sells no produce whatsoever.
Northgate Halal Market: Halal butcher and grocer. Lamb, goat and chicken slaughtered to halal standards. Does not sell pork or alcohol.
Thorne & Daughters: Village shop with a surprisingly good spice cabinet — whole cumin, cardamom, saffron, dried chiles. Produce is limited to onions and potatoes.
Meridian Organics: Certified organic grocer. All produce organic, no conventional. Does not carry any refined white sugar or white flour.
Foxglove Fine Foods: Specialty shop. Excellent olive oils and aged vinegars, imported anchovies, tinned fish. No refrigerated meat case.
Culver Street Co-op: Member co-op with strong bulk bins — oats, lentils, seeds, baking supplies. Explicitly does not stock bulk spices, only jarred.
Rivera Carnicería: Mexican butcher shop. Thin-cut beef, chorizo, carnitas, tripe. Sells masa and tortillas. Does not sell any Asian ingredients.
Blue Heron Market: Small-town grocery. Sells beer and wine but holds no spirits license — no liquor of any kind.
Ashford Naturals: Health food store. Good selection of gluten-free flours and alternative sweeteners. Sells no wheat products at all.
Kestrel Bakery & Grocer: Bread-focused shop with a small pantry. Sells fresh yeast and high-protein bread flour. Does not sell produce.
Tamarind Lane: Southeast Asian grocer. Fish sauce, tamarind paste, galangal, kaffir lime leaves, fresh herbs in bunches. No European goods.
Colbert's Dry Goods: Old-fashioned general store. Canned and shelf-stable only. Carries no refrigerated or frozen items — no fresh dairy.
Winterbourne Farm Stand: Seasonal stand, summer only. Sells tomatoes, sweet corn, squash and berries. No dairy, no meat, no pantry goods.
Orchard Gate Market: Suburban supermarket. Full grocery with a large kosher section. Sells no shellfish.
Pelletier Frères: French-leaning épicerie. Cultured butter, Dijon, cornichons, duck fat, good baguettes. Stocks duck fat year round.
Sunrise Convenience: Corner store. Chips, soda, candy, cigarettes, a cooler of beer. Does not sell fresh produce.
Hollowell Naturals: Vegan grocery. Cashew cheeses, oat milk, nutritional yeast, mock meats. Does not sell eggs or dairy.
Cedarwood Market: Upscale grocer. Excellent selection of local honey and maple syrup from within the state. Meat counter is small but good.
Portage Bay Grocery: Neighborhood store. Carries a wide range of dried beans and pulses in bulk. Explicitly does not stock any frozen foods.
Bellweather Provisions: Small market with a focused pantry. Sells whole-bean coffee roasted in-house. No tea beyond a few supermarket boxes.
Lindqvist Fisk: Scandinavian fishmonger. Cured and smoked fish, pickled herring, gravlax, cod roe. Sells no shellfish, no meat.
Grand Avenue Deli: Jewish-style deli and market. Smoked fish, rye bread, pickles, brisket. Does not sell pork products.
Fairhaven Bulk: Zero-waste bulk store, bring your own jars. Grains, flours, spices, oils and soaps dispensed by weight. Sells nothing packaged.
Crossroads Supermercado: Latino supermarket. Full carnicería, dried chiles by the bin, Mexican dairy. Good selection of Central American beers.
Aubrey's Corner Shop: Tiny urban market. Milk, eggs, bread, a few vegetables. No butcher counter and does not sell fresh meat.
Elmgrove Natural Market: Natural foods store. Extensive supplements and bulk herbs. Carries no alcohol and no tobacco.
Sablefish & Co.: Seafood market with a small retail pantry. Sells fish stock and fish bones for broth. No poultry or red meat.
Thistle & Thorn: Scottish-leaning import shop. Oats, black pudding, haggis in season, Scottish cheeses. Excellent single malt selection.
Marigold Market: Indian grocery. Whole spices, ghee, paneer, atta, lentils of every kind. Sells no alcohol.
Northern Pines Outfitter Store: Camp supply with a food aisle. Freeze-dried meals, jerky, canned goods. No fresh food of any kind.
Volkov Gastronom: Eastern European deli. Kielbasa, smetana, buckwheat, pickled vegetables, rye. Good selection of imported vodka.
Two Rivers Meat Locker: Custom meat processor and retail counter. Whole and half animals, game processing, sausage. Sells lard and beef tallow.
Larkspur Grocery: Small organic market. Carries fresh and dried pasta, imported tinned tomatoes. Does not stock any candy or soda.
Hollis Street Fish Market: Fishmonger with live tanks. Sells live crab and lobster year round. Carries no fillets of freshwater fish.
Golden Wheat Bakery Supply: Baking supply shop. Flours by the sack, chocolate in blocks, yeast, pans and molds. Sells no savory ingredients.
Quarry Hill Market: Mainstream grocery in a college town. Full liquor department including a good selection of local beers and small-batch gin.
Sereno Mercato: Italian import shop. Tinned San Marzano, dried pasta, Parmigiano, prosciutto. Does not sell fresh produce.
Bayview Asian Foods: Pan-Asian grocery. Rice by the sack, noodles fresh and dried, full aisle of sauces. Does not carry a butcher counter.
Fenwick Farm Dairy: Dairy store attached to a working farm. Raw milk, cream, butter, farmstead cheese, eggs. Nothing else.
Drummond's Discount Foods: Salvage grocery selling close-dated and overstock goods. Canned and boxed only. Does not sell fresh produce or meat.
Stillwater Provisions: Small-batch pantry shop. Fermented goods — miso, kimchi, vinegars, kraut — plus koji. Sells no fresh meat.
Cranfield Grocery: Suburban supermarket with a strict store policy against selling tobacco or alcohol. Otherwise a full-service grocery.
Palisade Produce: Wholesale produce house open to the public. Cases of vegetables and fruit only. No dry goods, no dairy, no meat.
Havenwood Market: General grocery with an unusually deep frozen section. Frozen berries, vegetables, seafood and dough. Fresh seafood is not sold here.
Oakfield Pantry: Village shop specializing in preserves. Jams, chutneys, pickles, honey, curds. Carries no refrigerated meat or fish.
